criteria.name: Tech Implementation
criteria.justification: MCP SDK 2.x Streamable HTTP correctly mounted with 7 tools, 88 passing pytest tests, hard budget ledger enforced, and real Nebius Nemotron execution loop demonstrate strong technical completeness; skeptic notes friction log reveals unresolved MCP SDK lifespan and Playwright fallback issues.

criteria.name: Design
criteria.justification: Dashboard delivers live learning curve chart, token cost panel, Alexa simulator, and stream feed but zero external user testing conducted; skeptic penalizes unverified 'live' claims and absent usability validation.

criteria.name: Potential Impact
criteria.justification: Measured $0.0238 spend across 5 real sites with second-run zero-LLM recipe learning shows compelling ROI and cost control; skeptic flags tiny sample size, unverified recipe-learning claim, and no external benchmark replication.

criteria.name: Quality of the Idea
criteria.justification: Approval gates, budget ledger, recipe caching, and honest friction log documenting MCP SDK 2.x session/Playwright snags prove creative safety architecture beyond a wrapper; skeptic questions reusability scope and whether documented snags remain unresolved.

criteria.name: Technological Implementation
criteria.justification: Live Nebius Token Factory integration with dual Nemotron models, verified token billing ($0.0238/41 calls), and 88 passing pytest tests demonstrate strong execution; supheci notes test coverage depth unverified.

criteria.name: Design
criteria.justification: Dashboard shows learning curve (calls→0 on replay), token savings panel, and live frame streaming — strong visual feedback; supheci penalizes absence of documented user testing.

criteria.name: Potential Impact
criteria.justification: Recipe caching and hard budget guards enable measurable cost reduction for repetitive web workflows; supheci flags 'drastic reduction' as unverified without live user deployment data.

criteria.name: Quality of the Idea
criteria.justification: Two-tier model routing (fast default, strong on failure) plus automated DOM recovery with CV fallback is a non-obvious, clever architecture; supheci questions production readiness of CV fallback.

criteria.name: Impact
criteria.justification: Human approval gates and domain allowlists provide a safety framework, but real-world validation and robustness of enforcement remain unverified.

criteria.name: Technical
criteria.justification: Multi-agent council mechanism and reasoning traces are implemented with 88 passing tests, though test coverage depth and consensus reliability need further scrutiny.

criteria.name: Innovation
criteria.justification: Zero-cost recipe caching and hard budget ceilings demonstrate cost-saving innovation, yet actual replay effectiveness and budget enforcement under load are unproven.

criteria.name: Demo
criteria.justification: Recorded video showcases dashboard and execution flow, but absence of live streaming endpoint and limited demo duration raise doubts about real-time performance.

criteria.name: Product & UX
criteria.justification: Interactive dashboard with runs overview, live screenshots, and budget metrics offers strong usability, though user testing evidence is lacking.

criteria.name: Sponsor Tech
criteria.justification: Integration with NVIDIA Nemotron on Nebius cloud is claimed, but technical depth of integration and open agent protocol adherence are not demonstrated.

criteria.name: Application of Technology
criteria.justification: Headless browser with HTTP fallback and Docker sandbox with resource limits show solid engineering, but simulated Vultr operations and absent unit tests/API completeness evidence reduce confidence in production readiness.

criteria.name: Presentation
criteria.justification: 62-second demo captures containment moment and docs/rules/vultr.md is complete, yet brevity limits technical depth and no live user testing footage leaves adoption friction unverified.

criteria.name: Business Value
criteria.justification: Hard budget caps ($0.50/day, $0.05/run), domain allow/deny lists, and approval gates directly address enterprise rogue-agent risk, but UX exposure of these guards and real-world deployment proof are missing.

criteria.name: Originality
criteria.justification: Blast_radius.json per-execution ledger tracking files, domains, duration, and USD is a novel containment artifact, though Docker sandboxing itself is established practice and marketing term 'Blast Radius Zero' outpaces independent verification.
